chapter: Small band, Charlie Parker and the big band
title: Taking the first group into the 2-10 Club
summary: Bales got him a spot at Martin's plaza club, the start of the 2-10; the first group had Gates, Popeye, Bob Mabane, Gene Ramey and his cousin Pete McShann.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: So well, he'd always have something to do, you know. He'd say -- I'd say, "Well, Mr. Bales, what are you doing?" He'd say, "Well, I don't know. Maybe we'll get together and run over a few tunes this evening." "Okay." So then he told me, he says, "You know, everybody kind of liked you over there. They liked you pretty good. So I know a guy over here, Martin, he's got a club over here on the plaza. There's never been no colored musicians in there, but I know him pretty well. Now, if you want to get a group together, take a group in there, I'll talk to him." I said, "Oh, yes, yeah." So he talked to Mr. Martin and the next thing I knew, I was taking a group in there, you know, and that was the starting of the 2-10, you know.
Well, the first bunch that I took in there was a guy we called Gates, old fella on trumpet, you know, and --
And I really can't think of his real name, but that was his nickname. All the musicians (inaudible).
Oh, that was a nickname, yeah.
That was a nickname, Gates. And I had Popeye, I had --
Popeye, he was a alto sax man. I had Popeye on the alto and I had a guy named Bob Mabane on tenor.
Oh, he was to stay with you quite a while.
Yes, Bob Mabane. Gene Ramey and -- let me see, the first drummer, and Pete McShann was the first drummer I had.
But he was in Kansas City, too?
Yes, he was in Kansas City, yes.
